text:
elaine: Heads-up — noticed a regression in the prefetch hit curve after last night's runtime roll. 95p token latency for /chat-stream jumped ~30ms and token-level breakdown shows a spike in KV cache misses around 02:10 UTC. :eyes:

mike: ugh, timeline? which change rolled?

elaine: infra-bot shows rollout of runtime-core v1.14.2 at 01:58 UTC (kernel_selector auto-v2 + new batching heuristic).

arjun: can you paste the PromQL you used for hit rate? want to check route-level split.

elaine: sure — pulled this from observability: 
```
# global prefix cache hit rate (rolling 5m)
sum(increase(kv_prefetch_hits_total[5m])) / (sum(increase(kv_prefetch_hits_total[5m])) + sum(increase(kv_prefetch_misses_total[5m])))

# per-route reuse (sample)
sum by(route) (increase(kv_prefetch_reuse_total[5m])) / sum by(route) (increase(kv_prefetch_requests_total[5m]))
```
Observed: global hit rate fell from ~0.86 -> 0.62 between 01:50–02:20. Top-traffic route (/chat-stream) reuse rate dropped from 0.74 -> 0.41.

mike: evictions? memory footprint change?

elaine: evictions spiked (~4.2k extra evictions across cluster in 20m). Memory usage didn’t increase — cache size steady at configured 120GB. Means policy/lookup pattern changed, not capacity.

arjun: I ran a quick profile on a box (perf + trace): kernel_selector path picked a different attention kernel for seq_len 1024 batches. That led to slightly longer per-step processing and we likely saw more interleaving of prefetch windows, causing evictions before reuse. Flamegraph shows increased time in attention::matmul_fused on auto-v2.

jess: so two hypotheses — kernel tradeoff increased latency causing longer kv lifetimes to be invalidated, or batching heuristic changed ordering so prefixes are not reused as much.

elaine: yeah. Also noticed batching windows tightened from 8ms -> 4ms in the new heuristic. Shorter windows reduced overlap of requests from same route, reducing reuse.

mike: can we simulate with old kernel_selector but new batching, and vice versa? quick A/B in a canary?

infra-bot: deploy canary started: runtime-core v1.14.2 (kernel_selector=auto-v2, batching_window=4ms) to canary pool 3 hosts.

arjun: good idea. I spun a local reproduce using rdw-sim and toggled two knobs. With kernel_selector=auto-v1 + batching_window=4ms hit rate stayed ~0.84. With auto-v2 + batching_window=8ms hit rate ~0.79. So primary regression vector looks like the kernel change, batching hits too but smaller delta.

jess: that suggests kernel selection changed memory access patterns so prefetch heuristics miss more.

mike: what about eviction policy? LRU vs segment-aware LRU? any route-level evictions concentrated on a few shards?

elaine: eviction heatmap shows evictions concentrated on shards serving high parallel fanout routes — /batch-infer and /chat-stream. Those routes interleave many short requests, the new kernel increases per-request processing time and causes more churn.

arjun: quick mitigation options:
- revert kernel_selector to auto-v1 for next rollout (fast)
- increase batching_window to 12ms to restore overlap (low risk, some latency impact)
- tune prefetch window / TTL on prefix cache for high-fanout routes (medium effort)

mike: also consider route pinning: mark high-reuse routes to use a sticky shard or increase per-route cache quota so they don't evict each other.

elaine: agree. For immediate SLAs I propose revert kernel_selector to auto-v1 cluster-wide and run targeted experiments for batching and prefetch TTL in canary. We should also add a per-route reuse panel to the console for 95/50/avg over time.

jess: +1, can we patch runtime config live?

infra-bot: kernel_selector override applied to cluster: runtime-core.kernel_selector=auto-v1 (rolling 10 hosts) — change started at 02:46 UTC.

sre-bot: alert resolved: kv-prefetch-hitrate-drop (fired 02:12 UTC) — now recovered to 0.85 at 02:55 UTC.

mike: nice. For follow-up tickets:
- add per-route reuse metric to route KPI dashboard (Elaine)
- add a rejection/eviction source label to evictions counter (Arjun)
- run controlled perf experiments to understand kernel memory access patterns (Mike + Arjun)
- evaluate route pinning or per-route quotas (Jess)

elaine: filing tickets now. Also adding perf artifacts to the runtime-issues board: small flamegraphs, PromQL queries, and sample request traces.

arjun: FYI I saved a short kernel diff that triggered selection change (link in thread). Will open PR to add a selection test that simulates seq_len variance so we don't regress reuse again.

mike: thanks — good triage. We'll keep monitoring per-route 95p and eviction spikes during next roll. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jess: please add a Canary checklist item: verify per-route reuse not regressing more than 5% vs baseline.

elaine: done. I'll post a short runbook for oncall if this repeats.

infra-bot: canary rollout fully reverted to kernel_selector=auto-v1 at 02:58 UTC.

sre-bot: closing incident (postmortem pending).
